title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays: binary search partition, O(log min(m,n)).
shortTitle: Median of Two Sorted Arrays: Binary Search Partition, O(log min(m,n))
keyPoints: Binary-search a partition in the smaller array so the left side holds exactly half the total elements.
The matching partition in the larger array is forced: j = halfTotal - i.
The crossing condition requires maxLeftA <= minRightB and maxLeftB <= minRightA.
For even total, the median is the average of max(leftA, leftB) and min(rightA, rightB); for odd, it is max(leftA, leftB).
Use negative and positive infinity sentinels when a cut lands at the start or end of an array.
Always search the smaller array to keep the complexity O(log min(m, n)) and avoid out-of-bounds cuts.
Use BigDecimal for boundary comparisons and averaging with a defined rounding mode for financial data.

s1_definition.oneliner: Binary-search a partition in the smaller array so left holds half the total and the boundary values cross correctly.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Median of Two Sorted Arrays** – finds the median of the combined sorted order of two already-sorted arrays without merging them.
- **Partition search** – binary-search a cut in the smaller array; the matching cut in the larger array is derived so the left side holds half the total elements.
- **Crossing condition** – `maxLeftA <= minRightB` and `maxLeftB <= minRightA` must both hold for a valid split.
- **O(log min(m, n)) time, O(1) space** – searching the smaller array keeps the tightest bound.
- **Infinity sentinels** – treat missing boundaries as negative or positive infinity to handle edge cuts uniformly.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India has two sorted lists of transaction amounts, Rajesh's and Priya's, and an analyst needs the median amount of both combined without merging them. Imagine drawing a vertical cut through each list so everything to the left of both cuts is the smaller half and everything to the right is the larger half. The analyst slides the cut in the smaller list, computing the matching cut in the larger, until the two halves balance perfectly, and reads the median off the boundary.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│   Median of Two Sorted Arrays: Partition Binary Search   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                          │
│  A (smaller): [ a0, a1, ..., a(i-1) | a(i), ..., a(m-1)]│
│  B (larger):  [ b0, b1, ..., b(j-1) | b(j), ..., b(n-1)]│
│                                                          │
│  Left half = A[0..i-1] + B[0..j-1]   (half elements)    │
│  Right half = A[i..m-1] + B[j..n-1]                     │
│                                                          │
│  Crossing condition:                                     │
│    maxLeftA <= minRightB  AND  maxLeftB <= minRightA     │
│                                                          │
│  If maxLeftA > minRightB → hi = i - 1 (took too many)   │
│  If maxLeftB > minRightA → lo = i + 1 (took too few)    │
│  If both hold → partition found, read median off edges   │
│                                                          │
│  Odd total:  median = max(maxLeftA, maxLeftB)            │
│  Even total: median = avg(max(lefts), min(rights))       │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Median of Two Sorted Arrays finds the median of the combined order of two already-sorted arrays without merging them, solved in O(log min(m, n)) time with O(1) space. The idea is a partition: pick a cut in the smaller array, and the matching cut in the larger is forced because the left side must hold exactly half the total elements.

You binary-search the cut in the smaller array and check a crossing condition: the largest element on the left of each array must not exceed the smallest element on the right of the other. If the left of the smaller is too big, move its cut left; if too small, move right. When both conditions hold, read the median off the boundary values.

The nuances are the infinity sentinels and always searching the smaller array. When a cut lands at the start or end of an array, treat missing boundaries as negative or positive infinity. Always search the smaller array so the derived cut never goes out of bounds.

In a banking project at the National Bank of India, this reports the median transaction amount across Rajesh's and Priya's separately sorted lists without the cost of merging huge lists on every request.

Remember one sentence: Binary-search a partition in the smaller array so the left side holds half the total elements and the crossing condition is satisfied, then read the median off the boundary.
